The '''Ugor homeworld''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Paradise system/Legends|Paradise system]]&mdash;known as J21-Z65 on most [[Star map/Legends|star charts]]<ref name="SH">[[Scavenger Hunt (adventure)|''Scavenger Hunt'']]</ref>&mdash;in the [[Airam sector/Legends|Airam sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], at [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] coordinates M-20.<ref name="teaoc" /> The [[Ugor/Legends|Ugor]] [[Species/Legends|species]] evolved on the world. Although knowledge of the planet had been lost by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[sentientologist]] [[Obo Rin]] speculated that conditions there must have been perfect to allow for large, unicellular beings like the Ugors to evolve. It must have had easily obtainable nutrients, for example, and an absence of predatory species.<ref name="GG4" />

The planet also had vast natural resources,<ref name="SH" /> which the Ugors used to develop new technologies. This preceded their philosophical development, however, and the species unwisely overpopulated the world and polluted it with industrial waste. Rather than rectify the situation, though, the Ugors evolved the ability to survive in such conditions.<ref name="GG4" />

After the Ugors developed [[Realspace/Legends|space]] flight and took to roaming their system on [[Starship/Legends|starships]], they blew their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] to pieces, along with the other worlds of the Paradise system, to make way for a [[Star system/Legends|system]]-spanning junkyard.<ref name="SH" /><ref name="GG4" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Ugor homeworld&mdash;as well as its ultimate fate&mdash;were first mentioned in [[Scavenger Hunt (adventure)|''Scavenger Hunt'']], an adventure scenario written by [[Brad Freeman]] for the [[West End Games]] ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' in [[1989]]. Other sources have repeated the story and added a few more details, although the world is still largely undescribed. The cover of [[Scavenger Hunt (adventure)|''Scavenger Hunt'']] mentions a "Paradise sector," although ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion]]'' have shown that this was a misprint for "Paradise system."
